transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Thank you. Well, I came in because... I'm having some trouble with my eating habits. Usually after everyone goes to bed, I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have some leftovers. But then I realize I’ve eaten half a tray of catered pasta from work, the dessert from a client dinner, and just whatever snacks were in the pantry, all in one sitting. It's getting to be a real problem.
When you find yourself eating all of that in one sitting, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Yes, that is exactly it. Once I start... especially if it's been a tense night with my husband... it feels like the decision-making part of me just goes offline. I just keep reaching for more food, even while I’m sitting there thinking to myself, "Patricia, stop, this is enough." But I just can't seem to make myself stop.
Do these episodes of eating large amounts of food cause you distress, or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Yes, they really do. I mean, I’m still keeping up with work, so that part of my life is okay. But... the mornings after these nights, I just feel so drained. And really ashamed. It's getting to the point where I've started skipping plans, like my yoga classes or just time I usually spend doing creative things. I just feel so awful the next day that I really don’t want to face anyone.
After these episodes of eating a lot in one sitting, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of that. I just... I just feel bad about it the next day, but I don't throw up or take anything. And honestly, I'm usually too tired to even think about exercising after. I just kind of sit with it.
How often do you find yourself having these episodes of eating a large amount of food in a short period, followed by feeling upset or guilty about it?
Well, for the last three months or so, it's been happening at least once a week. Usually it's after a bad argument or if I have a really late work event. And, um, some weeks it even happens twice.
During these episodes, do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than normal?

Yeah, definitely. I... I eat really fast during those times. Usually, I'm just standing at the kitchen island, or maybe I'm scrolling through work emails on my phone, and I eat so quickly that I barely even taste the food. It's like... sometimes I'll just look down and the containers are already empty, before I've even really registered what I was eating.

latest_inference.note: The patient confirmed eating much more rapidly than normal during the episodes, which supports the diagnosis of Binge Eating Disorder (F50.01). No behaviors such as self-induced vomiting, laxative use, or excessive exercise were reported, ruling out Bulimia Nervosa (F50.02) and Other Specified Eating or Feeding Disorder (F50.81). The frequency and distress associated with the episodes meet criteria for F50.01.
